title: Endogenous Endophthalmitis: The Ocular Emergency from Within
summary: Endogenous endophthalmitis (EE) is a vision-threatening intraocular infection resulting from the hematogenous seeding of the eye from a distant primary source. Unlike exogenous forms, EE requires a multidisciplinary approach to identify the systemic origin while managing aggressive ocular inflammation.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Endogenous Endophthalmitis (EE) occurs when microorganisms cross the blood-ocular barrier and proliferate within the vitreous or aqueous humor. It accounts for 2-8% of all endophthalmitis cases. It is often a harbinger of occult systemic disease and carries a significantly worse visual prognosis compared to exogenous endophthalmitis due to the virulence of the pathogens and the compromised health of the host.

branches: Gram (+) : Staph. aureus, Strep. pneumoniae, Group B Strep

sections.title: Risk Factors & Predisposing Conditions
content: Diabetes Mellitus (Most common systemic association)
Intravenous Drug Use (IVDU) - often associated with fungal/Bacillus
Indwelling catheters (Port-a-cath, Hemodialysis)
Immunosuppression (Chemotherapy, AIDS, Organ transplant)
Recent major surgery (Abdominal/Cardiac)
Endocarditis and Valvular heart disease
Liver abscess (Highly associated with Klebsiella)
Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) or Meningitis

sections.title: The Klebsiella Syndrome
content: Emerging hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (K1/K2 serotypes)
Classic Triad: Liver abscess, Meningitis, and Endophthalmitis
Hypermucoviscosity phenotype allows escape from phagocytosis
Requires immediate Abdominal Imaging (CT/US) if EE is suspected without source

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup: The 'Seek the Source' Protocol
content: Step 1: Immediate Ocular Tap (Aqueous and Vitreous) for Gram/GMS/PAS stain and Culture
Step 2: Obtain Blood Cultures (Aerobic/Anaerobic) from two different sites
Step 3: Collect Urine Culture and Throat/Sputum culture if symptomatic
Step 4: Systematic Imaging: Chest X-ray (Pneumonia/Abscess), Abdominal US/CT (Liver/Renal Abscess)
Step 5: Transthoracic (TTE) or Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE) to rule out Endocarditis
Step 6: PCR for 16S/18S rRNA if cultures are negative but clinical suspicion remains high

rows: Lacks systemic septic foci; steroid response
History of trauma to the other eye

sections.title: Systemic Antimicrobial Selection
content: Bacterial: Third-generation cephalosporins (Ceftriaxone 2g IV q12h) or Fluoroquinolones (Moxifloxacin 400mg) for high vitreous penetration.
Fungal (Candida): Loading dose Fluconazole (400-800mg) or Voriconazole (6mg/kg IV q12h).
Fungal (Aspergillus): Voriconazole is the gold standard due to superior penetration and survival benefits.
Duration: Usually 4-6 weeks depending on clearing of systemic focus.
Coordination: Infectious Disease (ID) consult is mandatory for all EE patients.

sections.title: Surgical Intervention: Pars Plana Vitrectomy
content: Indication: Severe vitritis preventing visualization, failure of IVT, or rapid progression.
Objective 1: Reduce microbial load and inflammatory cytokines.
Objective 2: Obtain large undiluted vitreous sample for diagnostics.
Objective 3: Clear media for better follow-up and monitoring.
Technique: 23/25G small-gauge PPV, core vitrectomy usually sufficient; avoid aggressive peripheral shave if retina is necrotic.

sections.title: Complications & Prognosis
content: Phthisis Bulbi (high risk in Gram-negative cases)
Tractional or Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment
Secondary Glaucoma (neovascular or inflammatory)
Evisceration/Enucleation required in 25% of Klebsiella cases
Poor Visual Outcomes: < 20/200 in ~60% of bacterial EE
Mortality: Significant risk due to underlying sepsis or endocarditis

content.explanation: P: Primary Source (Find it!), U: Unilateral/Bilateral? (Bilateral favors EE), M: Microbiology (Blood + Vitreous), P: Penetration (Systemic drugs must cross blood-eye barrier)

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & High-Yield Facts
content: Blood cultures are positive in up to 75% of EE, often higher than vitreous cultures.
In IVDU, think Bacillus cereus (explosive) or Candida (string of pearls).
Candida EE usually starts in the choroid and breaks into the vitreous.
Aspergillus EE often presents with a large subretinal abscess in the macula.
EVS (Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study) criteria DO NOT strictly apply to endogenous cases.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
sections.content: Recent literature highlights the increasing role of Intravitreal Voriconazole as a first-line agent for fungal EE due to its safety profile and broad coverage. Genomic sequencing (mNGS) is proving superior to traditional culture in culture-negative cases. Furthermore, early PPV (within 24-48 hours) is increasingly advocated for endogenous Klebsiella cases to save the globe, even if vision remains poor.
